The *Kappamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 14) is a canonical commentary belonging to the *Cūḷaniddesa* within the Khuddaka Nikāya. It provides a detailed, word-by-word doctrinal exposition (*niddesa*) of the verses comprising the *Kappamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.11 / PTS Snp 211) from the *Pārāyanavagga* of the *Sutta Nipāta*. Within the canonical and post-canonical corpus, the text is referenced or cross-noted in the *Anamatagga Saṁyutta* (*Tiṇakaṭṭhasutta*, SN 15.1), the *Peṭakopadesa* (*Suttavebhaṅgiya*, Pe 9), the *Kathāvatthu* (*Puggalakathā*, Kv 1.1), and related sections of the *Cūḷaniddesa* itself (Cnd 2).

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon, recording 1,144 matching passages shared with 66 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial text reuse occurs with the *Anamatagga Saṁyutta* (SN 15, sharing 48 matches totaling 6,647 characters, notably §6.2–6.5 aligned with SN 15 §19.1.6–19.1.10), as well as related exegetical treatises across both the *Cūḷaniddesa* (such as Cnd 12, Cnd 8, Cnd 9, Cnd 17, and Cnd 23) and the *Mahāniddesa* (e.g., Mnd 15 and Mnd 14) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant text-sharing with its traditional commentary, the *Cūḷaniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* (61 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies automatic cross-language alignments with Tibetan Buddhist texts, most notably the *Mūlamadhyamakavṛtti Akutobhayā* (D3829, best score 75; e.g., §6.2 aligned with §55a-33–55b-1) and the Tibetan translation of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (D0119-2) [DharmaNexus].
